merge_reason: Kept separate: this is a diagnostic acid-base/electrolyte and toxicology audit of acquired pseudo-Bartter syndrome, with different populations, tests, primary literature and safety outputs from request 0.
prompt: Required researcher: prochatgpt_researcher. Audit acquired pseudo-Bartter syndrome and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis in chronic diuretic use, misuse, vomiting/eating disorders, gastrointestinal chloride loss and heavy sweating, while differentiating inherited Bartter/Gitelman syndromes. Explain serum electrolytes/acid-base patterns, urine chloride and potassium timing, renin/aldosterone, magnesium, urine diuretic screens and false negatives after delayed sampling or replacement fluids. Contrast loop/thiazide/acetazolamide/potassium-sparing effects. Verify the counterexample that ordinary diarrhea or laxative-related bicarbonate loss more often produces metabolic acidosis, while mixed cases can occur. Use primary case reports/series, nephrology reviews, authoritative lab/toxicology references and current official medicine information; open underlying URLs rather than snippets. Search for direct lipedema relevance and say clearly if absent. Do not diagnose readers or provide home electrolyte correction or taper instructions. Identify urgent symptoms, clinician-supervised tests, confounders and contradictory older claims, and produce safe simple Spanish wording that does not imply pseudo-Bartter proves eating-disorder behavior. Return URLs/PMIDs/DOIs, evidence class, limitations, discarded marketing/noise and follow-up questions. [Request 1]
